question_bank.title: Alpha Decay — Physics Assessment
question_bank.description: TIE Physics competence 13.1.1 (Form IV extension / advanced).

questions.question_text: An alpha particle consists of:
questions.explanation: Alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus.

questions.question_text: In alpha decay, the mass number decreases by:
questions.explanation: Alpha emission removes four nucleons.

questions.question_text: Half-life is the time for:
questions.explanation: Statistical half of a large sample decays in one half-life.

questions.question_text: Alpha radiation has:
questions.explanation: Stopped by paper or skin.

questions.question_text: Radioactive decay of a single nucleus is random.
questions.explanation: Individual decay times cannot be predicted.

questions.question_text: Alpha decay increases the atomic number by 2.
questions.explanation: Atomic number decreases by 2 when helium nucleus is lost.

questions.question_text: Adding more atoms in the sim shows decay is:
questions.explanation: Large samples follow predictable averages.

questions.question_text: The daughter nucleus after alpha emission has atomic number reduced by:
questions.explanation: Two protons are removed with the alpha particle.

questions.explanation: Also written as ⁴₂He or α.

questions.question_text: Define half-life in one phrase.
questions.correct_answer: time for half the nuclei to decay
questions.explanation: Characteristic decay time for a radioisotope.

question_bank.title: Beta Decay — Physics Assessment
question_bank.description: TIE Physics competence 13.1.1 (Form IV extension / advanced).

questions.question_text: In beta-minus decay, a neutron becomes:
questions.explanation: Charge is conserved via electron emission.

questions.question_text: Beta decay changes the atomic number by:
questions.explanation: One proton gained or lost relative to beta type.

questions.question_text: The mass number during beta-minus decay:
questions.explanation: Nucleon count is unchanged.

questions.question_text: Carbon-14 dating relies on:
questions.explanation: C-14 decays to N-14 with known half-life.

questions.question_text: Beta particles are high-speed electrons (or positrons).
questions.explanation: Beta radiation is charged lepton emission.

questions.question_text: Beta radiation penetrates less than alpha radiation.
questions.explanation: Beta penetrates further than alpha; gamma penetrates most.

questions.question_text: Balanced nuclear equations require conserving:
questions.explanation: Total protons and nucleons must balance.

questions.question_text: Medical tracers may use beta emitters because:
questions.explanation: Short-lived isotopes image metabolic processes.

questions.question_text: Name the particle emitted in beta-minus decay.
questions.explanation: Also called a beta particle.

questions.question_text: What happens to the atomic number in beta-minus decay?
questions.explanation: Neutron converts to proton in the nucleus.

question_bank.title: Blackbody Spectrum — Physics Assessment
question_bank.description: TIE Physics competence 13.1.1 (Form IV extension / advanced).

questions.question_text: As temperature increases, the peak wavelength:

questions.explanation: Colour change reflects peak moving through visible band.

questions.question_text: Wien's Law relates peak wavelength to:
questions.explanation: Higher T means shorter peak wavelength.

questions.question_text: All objects above absolute zero emit electromagnetic radiation.
questions.explanation: Thermal radiation is universal.

questions.question_text: Cooler stars always peak at shorter wavelengths than hotter stars.
questions.explanation: Hotter stars peak at shorter wavelengths.

questions.question_text: The visible band overlay helps compare:

options: Different peak wavelengths at different temperatures
questions.correct_answer: Different peak wavelengths at different temperatures
questions.explanation: Temperature determines spectral shape.

questions.question_text: State how colour of a hot object changes as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Peak moves through visible spectrum.

questions.question_text: What does the height of the spectrum curve represent?
questions.explanation: Power emitted per wavelength interval.

question_bank.title: Circuit Construction Kit: AC — Physics Assessment
question_bank.description: TIE Physics competence 13.1.1 (Form IV extension / advanced).

question_bank.title: Quantum Measurement — Physics Assessment

question_bank.title: Quantum Wave Interference — Physics Assessment
question_bank.description: TIE Physics competence 13.1.1 (Form IV extension / advanced).

questions.question_text: The double-slit experiment demonstrates:
questions.explanation: Single quanta build interference over time.
